claim: *MAGE across the product lifecycle.* Different lifecycle surfaces ask different engineering questions and therefore benefit from different representations. The horizontal flow is not a waterfall: experience and evidence feed earlier activities, while Assurance & Compliance spans the lifecycle. Each surface can adopt MAGE independently.
topology:
Four recurring engineering activities run left to right as a dominant lifecycle flow: Product
    Discovery, Engineering and Realization, Product Management and Maintenance, and Operations and Incidents. Each
    box carries the question it asks and the representations it produces. Assurance and Compliance is drawn below,
    spanning the row as a cross-cutting activity that feeds up into all four. A wide arrow beneath the lifecycle row
    shows observations, failures, evidence, and new needs feeding back into earlier activities; the sequence is a
    lifecycle, not a waterfall.
required_terms: What should we build? Why? hypotheses · needs experiments · decisions requirements
How should it be realized? architecture · behavior interfaces · contracts analyses
What should change? Why? tickets · issues · rationale acceptance · history
What is happening? Why? topology · telemetry SLOs · runbooks · RCAs
Observations, failures, evidence and new needs feed earlier activities.
ASSURANCE & COMPLIANCE · cross-cutting What must be shown to be true? requirements · policies · threats · traceability · claims · evidence
